line_1.speaker: Corrin
line_1.text: Because thin enough, one lamp lights a city. I proved it on paper. On paper it is still true and that is where I should have left it.

line_2.speaker: Corrin
line_2.text: They were tuned to the angle of the light, not to any key. When the angle moved they went on singing. I could hear them from the workshop for a long time after that stopped making sense.

line_3.speaker: Corrin
line_3.text: Something. Nobody has ever shown it is the same light that went in, and I have stopped volunteering to be the one who checks.

gated.speaker: Corrin
gated.text: You have been in the caverns. That is the first cut, the coarse one. Everything I did was the same crime with a finer edge.

start.speaker: Corrin
start.text: Corrin the Lampwright has taken a corner of the tower and made it look lived in, which is more than the tower has managed on its own.

choices.text: Why did you cut it so thin?
I have been in the caverns.
Why keep the brackets up at all?

corrin_service.speaker: Corrin
corrin_service.text: Wax off the chapel candles. It burns badly and it burns for a very long time, which is the only quality that matters below the fourth floor.

corrin_arc.speaker: Corrin
corrin_arc.text: Because a bracket with nothing in it is still a bracket, and the day somebody comes up the stair with a full lamp there will be somewhere to put it. That is the whole of my reasoning and I am aware of how it sounds.
